chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Uqba, from his father, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'The look is a poisoned arrow from the arrows of Iblis, and how many looks have caused prolonged regret.'

key_terms.إِبْلِيسَ: Iblis (Satan), the source of this spiritual poison.
key_terms.النَّظَرُ: The look or gaze, specifically referring to the act of looking with intent or lust.
key_terms.حَسْرَةً: Regret or remorse, specifically spiritual or emotional regret.
key_terms.سَهْمٌ: Arrow, used metaphorically for a weapon or instrument of harm.
key_terms.طَوِيلَةً: Long or prolonged, describing the duration of the regret.
key_terms.مَسْمُومٌ: Poisoned, indicating the harmful nature of the gaze.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the 'look' (al-nazar) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) characterizes the lustful gaze as a 'poisoned arrow' from Iblis, highlighting its role as a primary gateway for spiritual corruption and lasting regret. This metaphor underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on 'gharaz al-nazar' (directed looking) as an active spiritual struggle that can derail one's devotion and lead to prolonged remorse.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ali Bin Uqba, from his father, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,
‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The (lustful) look is a poisoned arrow from the poisoned arrows of Iblees<sup>la</sup>, and how many from the looks have caused prolonged regrets’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from Ali ibn ‘Uqbah from his father who has said the following: “
I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘Looking is an arrow of the poisoned arrows of Satan, and there are many such arrows that cause regret for a long time.’”
